column1: There's a magnet in your pocket right now.
When your phone buzzes, that's a tiny motor spinning... and inside it sits a tiny, very strong magnet.
Now check the spec sheet of an electric scooter or car.
Look at the motor line, and you'll often see two words... permanent magnet.
Same family of magnet, just bigger.
No magnet, no motor.
No motor... no E.V.
And in twenty twenty-five, that one magnet hit India's E.V. makers hard.
July, Pune.
Bajaj's electric Chetak factory was making barely half the scooters it made a year earlier.
The reason?
Not a strike.
Not batteries.
That small magnet... and most of them come from China.
In July twenty twenty-four, about twenty thousand Chetaks a month.
In July twenty twenty-five... less than eleven thousand.
And the crazy part?
The raw material for that magnet is lying in the sand on our own beaches — in Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Odisha.
By our own government's count, India's sands hold about seven million tonnes of rare earths.
So why can't India make the magnet?
Stay with me, and you'll see three things.
The hard step nobody else wanted to do.
Then, about five minutes in, the secret inside our sand that kept it locked away.
And at the end, the date you should watch.
